clue.text: Senior nurse in Leeds is terrible

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of words Leeds is terrible, spanning their joins

explanation.surface: A Leeds hospital's nursing standards are under attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like part of the place name phrase, but it signals that the answer is concealed across the end of Leeds, all of 'is' and the start of terrible.
explanation.definitionFit: In British hospitals a sister is the senior nurse in charge of a ward.

clue.text: Angry about note that Twist requested

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the angry word goes round the note

parts.note: sore means angry or resentful
a memo is a short written note

explanation.surface: Someone cross about a note, which turns out to be Oliver Twist asking for more.
explanation.walkthrough: Oliver Twist, in Dickens's novel, famously asks the workhouse master 'Please, sir, I want some more'.
explanation.definitionFit: Oliver Twist's famous plea for extra gruel is for 'some more', so the phrase is what he requested.

clue.text: Son heading for difficult situation at traffic signal

parts.note: heading for means going to, so it gives TO
a plight is a difficult situation

explanation.surface: A son finds himself in trouble at a set of traffic lights.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoplight is a red traffic light, the signal that tells drivers to halt.

clue.text: Slippers in baskets, hiding first pair

indicators.note: hiding the first pair means the opening two letters of the baskets word are concealed and dropped

parts.note: creels are wicker baskets used by anglers

explanation.surface: Slippers tucked away in baskets, the first pair out of sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slippers' looks like footwear, but it is a playful definition of slippery creatures.
explanation.definitionFit: Eels are notoriously slimy and hard to hold, so they are things that slip away.

clue.text: After comeback concert, man takes fashionable drug

indicators.note: after places the man part following the reversed concert
a comeback is a return, so the concert word is read backwards

parts.note: a prom is a promenade concert

indicators.note: takes means the man word holds the fashionable word inside it

parts.note: he is a pronoun standing for a man
in means fashionable

explanation.surface: After a comeback gig, a man takes a trendy drug.
explanation.definitionFit: Morphine is a powerful opiate painkiller, a narcotic drug.

clue.text: Exposed, say, climbing the far boundary

parts.note: outed means exposed, especially publicly revealed

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue means the letters are read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: e.g. means for example, as does say

explanation.surface: Someone exposed while climbing toward a distant boundary.
explanation.definitionFit: An outedge is the outermost limit of something, its extreme border.

clue.text: Irritating typo on menu back

indicators.note: irritating suggests something stirred up and disturbed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An annoying misprint on a restaurant menu.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' sounds like the reverse side of a menu, but it is the definition, in the gambling sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To back a horse or team is to bet on it, which is to put money on it.

clue.text: Shackles Jeremy?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: chains or fetters for a prisoner
second meaning: Jeremy ... is an English actor, the question mark showing a definition by example

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that Jeremy is a name to be completed with a surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Fetters made of metal are called irons, and the actor Jeremy bears the same word as his surname.

clue.text: Progressive group starts to attract support round city in Texas

parts.note: ELP is Emerson, Lake and Palmer, a 1970s progressive rock band

indicators.note: starts to means the opening letters of attract and support are taken

parts.note: O is round in shape, so it stands for round

explanation.surface: A progressive political group begins to win backing around a Texan city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Progressive' suggests politics, but it is progressive rock: Emerson, Lake and Palmer were known as ELP.
explanation.definitionFit: El Paso is a large city in west Texas on the Mexican border.

clue.text: Unattractive people from America accepting German position

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the America letters hold the others

parts.note: US is the abbreviation for the United States, America
the lie of something is its position, as in the lie of the land

explanation.surface: Plain people from America accept a German post.
explanation.definitionFit: Uglies is an informal plural noun for ugly or unattractive persons.

clue.text: Spooner's diver could have another job

indicators.note: Spooner's signals swapping the opening sounds of two words, after Rev. Spooner

parts.note: a loon is a diving bird, called a diver in Britain
might means could

explanation.surface: A diver who could, according to Spooner, take on a second job.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the L and M of LOON MIGHT gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To moonlight is to work a second job on the side, often secretly, besides a main occupation.

clue.text: Old village puts pressure on god

indicators.note: on in an across clue means the pressure letter is placed after the god

parts.note: Thor is the Norse god of thunder
P is the physics abbreviation for pressure

explanation.surface: A god under pressure in an ancient settlement.
explanation.definitionFit: Thorp is an archaic word for a hamlet, surviving in English place names.

clue.text: A lot of yards being 50% camomile

indicators.note: fifty per cent means half of the word camomile is taken, its second half

explanation.surface: Half a tea blend of camomile, with yards thrown in.
explanation.walkthrough: Camomile has eight letters; its back half gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The imperial distance unit equals 1,760 yards, so the definition is a playful description by measurement.

clue.text: Amazing slideshow featuring last of your Mustangs?

indicators.note: amazing hints at a maze, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be jumbled

indicators.note: last of means the final letter of your

parts.note: the final letter of your is R

explanation.surface: An amazing slideshow featuring your Ford Mustangs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mustangs' looks like the car, but the question mark points to the untamed horses of the American West.
explanation.definitionFit: Mustangs are feral horses of the western United States, an example of untamed equines.

clue.text: It's sweet I'm cold outside, admits burglar evenly

indicators.note: outside means the cold sound wraps around the rest

parts.note: brr is the shivering exclamation for I'm cold
owns means admits, as in owning up

indicators.note: evenly means the even-numbered letters of burglar, second, fourth and sixth

explanation.surface: A sweet admitted by a shivering burglar.
explanation.walkthrough: BRR goes outside OWNS plus UGA (the even letters of burglar).
explanation.definitionFit: Brown sugar is partly refined cane sugar, a sweetener with molasses colour.

clue.text: Looks at fish eaten by communists

indicators.note: eaten by means the fish goes inside the communists

parts.note: Reds is a common name for communists
a gar is a long-snouted fish

explanation.surface: Someone studies fish being eaten by communists.
explanation.definitionFit: To regard something is to look at or consider it closely.

clue.text: Free former politician abducted by alien

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: abducted by means the politician is carried off inside the alien

parts.note: ET is the film extraterrestrial, an alien
MP stands for Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A former politician kidnapped by an alien and freed.
explanation.definitionFit: To be exempt is to be free from an obligation or liability that applies to others.

clue.text: Post-war lunch reported bit by bit

indicators.note: reported means as said aloud, so the phrase heard gives the answer

parts.note: a lunch after a war could be a peace meal

explanation.surface: An account of a lunch after the war, given in instalments.
explanation.definitionFit: Piecemeal means done gradually, a piece at a time, rather than all at once.

clue.text: Familiar with conditions outside ruined Troy

indicators.note: ruined means wrecked, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: t is a dictionary abbreviation for troy, the weight system

explanation.surface: Getting used to life outside the ruins of Troy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' looks like a containment signal, but it is anagram fodder rearranged as 'ruined' says, giving USEDTOI; T, from Troy, follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To be used to it is to be accustomed, having adjusted to the circumstances.

clue.text: Speech beginning as follows: "Shut up"

indicators.note: beginning means the first letter of speech

parts.note: to wit means namely, introducing what follows

explanation.surface: A speech that starts with an order to be quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: Stow it is a slang command meaning be quiet or stop talking.

clue.text: Collection of icons also left on counter

parts.note: too means also
a bar is a counter where drinks are served

explanation.surface: Religious icons also left on a shop counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'icons' suggests religious images, but these are computer icons.
explanation.definitionFit: A toolbar is a strip in a software window holding buttons for commands.

clue.text: Force brings down violas?

parts.note: F is the physics abbreviation for force
lowers means brings down

explanation.surface: A force knocks over some stringed instruments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'violas' looks like the instrument, but viola is also a plant genus, including pansies; the question mark signals an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Violas are garden plants grown for their blooms, so they are examples of these.

clue.text: Quite crafty, absorbing atmosphere

indicators.note: absorbing means taking in, so the crafty word holds the atmosphere

parts.note: fly is British slang for knowing or crafty
air means atmosphere

explanation.surface: Someone rather cunning soaks up the mood.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang, fly means sharp and streetwise.
explanation.definitionFit: Fairly means to a moderate degree, as in fairly good, reasonably.

clue.text: Country with roughly nothing Spanish

parts.note: ca is short for circa, meaning roughly
nada is Spanish for nothing

explanation.surface: A country with almost nothing Spanish about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Canada is a large North American nation, north of the United States.

clue.text: Serious complaint when boss's tie is undone

parts.note: as means when, as in 'as I left'

indicators.note: undone describes a tie loosened, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something serious happens when the boss's tie comes loose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is only a link word; the apostrophe S of boss's counts as a letter of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Asbestosis is a serious lung disease caused by inhaling asbestos fibres.

clue.text: Maybe boxer attacked children

parts.note: bit means attacked with teeth

explanation.surface: A boxer who attacked some children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxer' looks like a fighter, but it is the dog breed; 'Maybe' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A female dog is called this, and a boxer is a breed of dog, so a female boxer qualifies.

clue.text: Finally found purple bra fitted perfectly

indicators.note: finally means the last letters of the next four words are taken

explanation.surface: At last someone found a purple bra that fitted perfectly.
explanation.definitionFit: Dead as an adverb means exactly or completely, as in dead right or dead centre.

clue.text: Possibly retaining western influence

indicators.note: retaining means holding inside, so the western letter goes into the other word

parts.note: say means possibly or for example, as in 'say, ten'

explanation.surface: Perhaps keeping Western influence.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold sway is to have power or control over others.

clue.text: Spacesuit feature — superclean tight trousers

indicators.note: trousers is a verb here meaning pockets or takes in, so the answer is held within the words

explanation.surface: A spacesuit with very clean tight trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trousers' looks like a garment, but as a verb it means pockets, and it signals letters held inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An anti-g suit protects astronauts and pilots against the effects of high acceleration.

clue.text: Freezing boozer? Well, almost ghastly

indicators.note: ghastly means horrible, so the letters are mangled into a new order
almost means all but the last letter of well

explanation.surface: A freezing pub, almost ghastly enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims Well to WEL; that and BOOZER are rearranged as 'ghastly' signals. A boozer is British slang for a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Below zero describes temperatures under freezing point on the Celsius scale.

clue.text: Increase radio audience — sounds like they stick!

indicators.note: sounds like means the phrase said aloud gives the answer

parts.note: to increase a radio audience is to add hearers

explanation.surface: A radio station boosting listeners, which proves sticky.
explanation.definitionFit: Adherers are things or people that cling fast, as glue adheres.

clue.text: Sounds like key opening

indicators.note: sounds like means the word for key said aloud gives the answer

parts.note: a key is a low island, as in Florida Keys, so an islet

explanation.surface: Something that sounds like a key opening a lock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'key' looks like a door key, but it is a small island, as in the Florida Keys.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyelet is a small hole, often reinforced, for a lace or cord to pass through.
